archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran rhythm distributor)
archetype.definition: An 18th-year pocket passer who rarely scrambles or gets sacked, wins from the pocket on timing between the numbers, and this year has been asked to throw shorter and less often than in his big 2025.

report.headline: A good, not great, Stafford whose supporting cast just disappeared
report.take:
Stafford arrived in 2026 off one of the best years of his career: 46 touchdowns (first in the league), 0.228 EPA per play (8th) and a 6th-ranked success rate. This year is a clear step down but not a collapse. He sits at 0.122 EPA per dropback (18th of 55), still 0.148 above the qualifier average, with a 7.05 YPA that ranks 23rd. That is roughly his 2023-24 level, and that level has defined most of his Rams tenure. The 2025 season looks like the outlier, not this one.

The change is in how he plays. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, fell 5.9 points from last season to 13.44, and his intended air yards sit at 7.63, short of the sticks by 1.15. For a stretch from Week 6 to Week 8 he was living around 4-5 intended air yards a game. The offense still works because the protection and the middle of the field hold up. He is pressured on only 16.3% of dropbacks (7th fewest) and sacked on 3.9% (7th). His 10-to-19-yard throws return 0.319 EPA, the best zone on his chart. In the red zone he has 16 touchdowns against one interception at 0.317 EPA a play. The deep ball is gone, though: 27.8% completions, -9.6 CPOE and three picks on 36 attempts.

The record hides how much of this the defense is carrying. The Rams have won four of the last five while he averaged 210.2 yards a game, with the 4th-ranked defense and 6th-ranked rushing EPA doing the heavy lifting. His big yardage games came early, in shootouts and catch-up scripts at Denver and against Buffalo. The interceptions are the other thing to watch. He has 10, which ranks 51st of 55, and he is throwing one a game against 0.47 last year, even though his bad-throw rate actually improved from 17.4% to 15.9%. Some of that looks like bad luck on catchable-ball mistakes. But interceptions have always come with him (17 in 2021), and five of them came on intermediate throws, his best-paying area. That is the price of the throws that make the offense go.

The bigger story now is personnel. Puka Nacua is done for the season after MCL surgery. Davante Adams is on IR and more likely back in mid-December than Week 13. Terrance Ferguson won't return. Nacua and Adams were the only two targets producing real value: 19.5 and 17.2 EPA, with Adams at 0.352 per target. What remains is Tyler Higbee (0.144 per target), Kyren Williams (-0.016) and Konata Mumpfield (-0.02). Starting center Coleman Shelton and guard Steve Avila are also out for Green Bay. The efficiency floor of a smart veteran in a McVay offense stays. The ceiling drops until Adams returns.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, almost no sacks
strengths.body: He is pressured on few dropbacks and sacked on even fewer, both top-7 marks. That comes from quick processing (2.7-second time to throw) behind a line that ranks 8th in hit rate allowed. His pressure-to-sack rates have been strong the last two years too, so this is skill as much as blocking. It gets tested with two interior starters out.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle is the engine
strengths.body: His 10-to-19-yard throws are the most productive part of his game, at 0.319 EPA and a 58.8% success rate, and throws to the middle return 0.254 EPA. This is the classic Stafford timing-and-anticipation zone. It held up through his career and should survive the receiver losses better than anything vertical.

strengths.title: Finishing drives in the red zone
strengths.body: He has 16 red-zone touchdowns against one interception, at 0.317 EPA a play with a +3.5 CPOE. His touchdown rate is a point above the league average. Some of that will cool, but the Rams' rushing efficiency and his precision in tight areas make him a real scoring threat inside the 20.

concerns.title: His two best targets are gone
concerns.body: Nacua is out for the year and Adams is unlikely back before mid-December. Together they produced nearly all of the passing game's positive target value. The healthy options grade as roughly break-even per target outside of Higbee. That is a role and personnel problem, not a skill decline, but it caps his yardage and explosive plays for weeks.

concerns.title: Interceptions running hot
concerns.body: He is throwing one interception a game, up 0.53 from last season, and ranks 51st of 55 in picks. His bad-throw rate improved, so part of this should regress. But eight of his ten came on throws of 10+ air yards, and turnovers have been part of his game for years.

concerns.title: Third downs and the deep ball
concerns.body: On third down he is at -0.125 EPA with a 37.9% conversion rate, facing 7.2 yards to go on average. His deep throws have collapsed to a -9.6 CPOE. Both reflect an offense that has stopped attacking vertically, and neither is likely to improve without Nacua and Adams.

trend.note: By EPA, his games swing between clunkers (Week 1, Week 8) and big days (Weeks 2, 5 and 10), with no steady climb. Over the last three his efficiency per dropback edged up while his yardage fell 51 a game and his CPOE dipped 3.1, as the Rams leaned on defense and the run.

nextGame.headline: Thin receiver room and patched interior line meet a solid pass defense
nextGame.body:
Green Bay's pass defense ranks 8th by EPA and allows the 3rd-lowest explosive pass rate. It holds quarterbacks to 13.6 PPR points a game, 5th-fewest. That fits poorly with a Stafford who now lacks his vertical and YAC threats. The openings are at receiver, where the Packers give up more than usual to a team's WR1, and wide receivers draw an above-average share of the targets against them. Whoever becomes the top wideout could see volume. The tight end route looks closed, since Green Bay ranks 1st at holding TE1s under their averages. The game script should favor patience: Green Bay's offense ranks last in rushing EPA and plays without Josh Jacobs, while the Rams' defense ranks 4th. That points to a low-scoring game controlled by the Rams, which lines up with the 43.5 total.

Availability cuts both ways. The Rams play without Nacua and Adams, and without center Coleman Shelton and guard Steve Avila, starters at 92% and 91% of snaps. Interior pressure is the biggest threat to a pocket passer with no escape. On the other side, linebacker Zaire Franklin (99% of snaps) is listed out and Isaiah McDuffie is questionable, which could soften the short middle where Stafford likes to work. Micah Parsons is out, but he hasn't played this season, so his absence is already built into Green Bay's numbers. The game is indoors, and the Rams have 10 days of rest.

keyMatchups.title: Backup interior line vs pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Stafford's low sack rate rests on clean pockets. With two interior starters out, Green Bay's 12th-ranked sack rate becomes more dangerous. If the middle collapses, the timing throws he relies on go with it.

keyMatchups.title: Short middle without Franklin
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's linebacker group is thinned, with Franklin out and McDuffie questionable. That should help underneath throws to Williams and the slot. Green Bay limits explosive passes, so expect a methodical, short-area plan rather than shots.

keyMatchups.title: Packers can't run, Rams can wait
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay's rushing offense ranks last by EPA, and the Rams' defense ranks 4th. Stafford may not need volume to win this, which supports the team but limits his counting stats.

nextGame.watch: Who becomes his top target, and whether the patched interior line keeps his sack rate near its usual low level.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the efficient-but-modest version of Stafford to continue, with less juice until Adams returns. The skills that held across seasons should last: sack avoidance, intermediate accuracy and red-zone precision. The volume will not. The Rams' defense and run game let McVay keep attempts down, and without Nacua there is no target who reliably turns short throws into yards. I project 205-250 passing yards a game and 1.2-1.8 touchdowns a game. If Adams comes back healthy in mid-December, the top of that range opens up again.

The interception rate should come down somewhat toward the 0.6-1.0 a game range, given his improved bad-throw rate. His touchdown efficiency in the red zone is likely to cool a little too. Overall, think 12-17 fantasy points a game: still a functional starter, but no longer the high-ceiling passer of 2025.
swingFactors: Timing and health of Adams's return from IR
Shelton and Avila returning to the interior line
Whether the defense keeps game scripts run-heavy

confidence.note: Ten games of a stable profile, but the loss of his top two receivers is a fresh role change.
